newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's 3rd mobile licence tender to open in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Italy's 3rd mobile licence tender to open in Sept.

text.p: The tender for Italy's third mobile phone licence will open in September, Italy's Post and Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico said on Tuesday.
The Personal Communications Network (PCN) licence is due to be awarded in December and will be the third cellular phone licence to operate within Italy.
Maccanico said he also hoped to announce rules next month for the introduction of the DECT (Digital European Cordless Telephony) supercordless telephone service for urban areas.

Albacom, a joint-venture between British Telecom, Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, state-controlled oil giant ENI and Italian broadcaster Mediaset, has already said it will present a bid for the third licence.
Germany's Deutsche Telekom together with Italian electricity utility ENEL have also indicated that they are interested.
The tender was due to be offered earlier this year but was postponed for technical reasons.
Some of the companies interested in the licence have complained that the delay has allowed Italy's existing mobile phone firms to strengthen their market position.

Italy currently has two Global Systems Mobile (GSM) phone operators -- state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) and Omnitel, managed by information technology group Olivetti through an international consortium.
Both TIM and Omnitel are interested in DECT technology and Italy's state-controlled fixed line operator Telecom Italia said last year it wanted to set up a DECT service.

Italy's anti-trust body in May criticised the government for delays in approving rules for frequency band access to DECT and also said it saw "serious dangers" if public operators were allowed to maintain a long-term monopoly in the sector.
"By September the cabinet will open the tender for the third mobile phone licence. I hope at the same time to announce the date and conditions for the DECT," Maccanico said on Tuesday.
"Working together with the antitrust we will try and guarantee the conditions for free competition," he added.
Telecom Italia, which controls TIM, is due to be privatised in October.
